title: Sample-efficient A/B runway with adaptive bias-correction for model versioning
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a sample-efficient A/B testing runway for model variants that minimizes customer exposure while enabling statistically confident decisions and automated rollback. The feature should support canaries, parallel A/B arms, shadow-only traffic, and an adaptive allocation algorithm that corrects for covariate bias (time-of-day, region, device) to reduce false positives. The system integrates with Redwood Console for experiment creation, monitoring, and audit logs, and with the routing layer to apply dynamic sample allocation and deterministic fallback when metrics lag.

Scope: experiment setup UI and API, server-side adaptive allocator, sequential statistical checks (Bayesian posterior and frequentist optional), auto-rollback triggers, telemetry hooks for Console dashboards, and e2e tests. Excludes model training, long-term metric store (will use existing analytics pipelines), and SLA billing changes.

Why this work: Current manual rollouts are either too conservative (slow) or too risky (high exposure). Teams need a fast way to validate model changes for business metrics and latency while limiting user impact and operational overhead. Adaptive bias correction increases power for the same exposure budget by balancing arms against observed covariate drift.
acceptance_criteria: Console: create an experiment with control and 1..3 treatment arms, choose primary/secondary metrics, and enable adaptive bias-correction toggle
API: start/stop experiments and read current allocation and stats via REST endpoints
Router: can apply dynamic sample allocation decisions and fall back to fixed percentages if metrics delayed > 2 minutes
Sequential safety checks: support both Bayesian posterior probability thresholds (default 0.975) and optional frequentist group-sequential checks
Auto-rollback: experiment triggers an automatic rollback when a predefined safety signal is exceeded and writes a reversible audit record
Observability: Console shows real-time allocation, exposure, metric deltas, p-values/posterior, and suggested action (continue/stop/rollback)
E2E tests: integration test that runs a simulated experiment on staging with synthetic traffic and validates early-stop and rollback flow
Docs: PRD and runbook linked in ticket and a short Console UX guide in the product docs
notes: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with Eng and Design. Agreed to prioritize sample efficiency and operational safety over fully custom statistical tooling in phase 1.
2025-02-20: Eng recommended Bayesian sequential checks for smaller sample sizes; PM prefers providing both with Bayesian as default for ease-of-use.
2025-02-26: Trade-off: adaptive allocation increases interim bias risk; mitigation is to use covariate-adjusted estimators and conservative burn-in (min 1,000 requests per arm).
2025-03-03: Agreed guardrails: max exposure per experiment 15% by default, can be increased by SRE/Enterprise sales on a per-customer basis.
Implementation choices: use existing stats-service for aggregation (ENG-20912) and extend router API (ENG-21098) for allocation signals. Design will reuse rollout UI patterns from runtime rollouts.
